analysis: Examined the scripts/test-release-dev-branch.py rewrite: the base text, the head text and the patch. The base test pinned a dispatch-only, ad-hoc-signed dev-branch lane. It forbade Apple and Developer ID secrets and kept secrets out of the job that builds branch code (base 60-68, 94-100). The head test pins a different lane: push-to-dev only, calling ./.github/workflows/release-provider.yml with environment dev and `secrets: inherit` (head 97-141). That workflow signs with the Developer ID, notarizes and staples (head 201-205). Head 180-199 lets the signing job read the Apple signing set unguarded. Prod and staging secrets are excluded only by the needs.resolve-env expression guard, with no GitHub environment attached (head 199). One finding records the change in signing-credential custody (T-054/T-034/A-017). Coverage limits: release-dev-branch.yml, release-provider.yml, release-swift.yml and the resolve-env job are not in this batch. I could not verify three things here: whether `dev` has branch protection, whether resolve-env can be steered to prod/staging from a dev push, or whether coordinator qualification (A-017, TB-011) rejects Team-ID-signed dev builds. Integration should check four further points. First, whether the GUARDED_SECRET regex (head 41-43) covers every prod/staging secret read. Second, whether the signing job executes branch code before or after importing the p12. Third, whether publish-release uses only DEV_RELEASE_KEY on the dev path (head 215-221). Fourth, whether the uses: local path (head 127-128) means the reusable workflow is the dev branch's own copy, which is editable by dev pushers. If it is, every secret passed by `secrets: inherit` is reachable from dev, prod included.

findings.detail: The base test treated a credential-free build job as a trust boundary. Base lines 94-100 required that the job compiling branch code reference no secret. It also banned APPLE_CERTIFICATE, DEVELOPER_ID and notarization (base 60-68). The head test reverses this. Head lines 4-7 and 15-17 say a push to `dev` runs the reusable release-provider.yml. Its `build-and-release` job builds the pushed commit and receives APPLE_CERTIFICATE_P12, its password, the provisioning profile and the Apple ID/app password (head 35-39, 193-197). Head 201-205 pins a Developer ID signature, notarization and stapling. Head line 199 asserts that the reusable workflow attaches no GitHub `environment:`. The caller passes `secrets: inherit`, and head 138 pins that. Prod and staging secrets are therefore filtered only by the in-file expression guard (head 41-43), not by environment protection rules. Trigger: anyone able to push to `dev` alters a build script, SwiftPM plugin or test that runs in the signing job. Impact: the code can read or exfiltrate the p12, or obtain an official, notarized Team-ID signature on unreviewed code. That weakens the official-build identity that T-034/T-054 and A-017 qualification rely on, and the fan-helper team requirement (TB-010). Fix options: keep signing secrets in a separate job that never runs branch code; gate dev signing behind a protected GitHub Environment with branch protection on `dev`; or use a distinct dev signing identity. Update the threat model so it states that Developer ID custody now extends to the dev branch.
findings.title: Dev-branch lane now gives dev-pushed code the Developer ID signing and notarization credentials
